chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Similar to it, indicating the content matches a previously mentioned narration

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'Similar to it' from Imam Abu Ja'far refer to in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) reinforces the theological foundation of Sabr (patience) by linking it directly to the concept of Rujoo' (returning to Allah), a core tenet in Shia eschatology. It contextualizes the verse 2:156 not merely as a phrase of consolation, but as an affirmation of divine ownership and ultimate accountability, urging believers to maintain composure through the lens of Tawhid. This connection highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating verbal remembrance with internal spiritual acceptance during trials.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from abu Jamilah, from Jabir from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
